paragraphs: Fourth-year Computer Science student at Canadian University Dubai (GPA 3.97, graduating Dec 2027). I build applied AI and LLM features, cloud data pipelines and machine-learning models, and I don't stop at "it runs": I measure whether the numbers are right.

In practice that means scoring an AI model's estimates against what users actually saved, reconciling every backfilled chunk of a pipeline against its source, and publishing the coverage gap next to the finding it qualifies.
features: React 19 TypeScript FastAPI PostgreSQL SQLAlchemy Gemini PWA

A deployed multi-user calorie and macro tracker, formerly Macros Calculator. It started in 2024 as a single-user Streamlit prototype and was rebuilt as a React SPA over a FastAPI REST API. 200+ merged PRs · 1,600+ tests…

Multimodal AI meal analysis (Gemini) — describe a meal, record a voice note, or photograph it. A voice note becomes editable text before anything is estimated, so a misheard ingredient is a typo to fix, not a wrong…

Your foods, the AI's eyes: attach saved foods and their macros are sent as facts — the AI estimates the portion, your library supplies the macros. A photo with no note is asked about hidden oil and sauces first, because…

The model's accuracy is measured, not assumed. Every estimate is logged and compared against what the user actually saved — interval coverage and directional bias per macro, with sample sizes — and it refuses to report…
